The Best Electric Motorcycle Routes in the UK for 2026

Electric motorcycles have quietly come of age, and planning the best electric motorcycle routes in the UK is now more about savouring the silence than sweating over the battery. That said, riding electric does demand a different mindset. You plan around real-world range, you build the day around sensible charge stops, and you learn to love the whisper-quiet torque that makes twisty roads such a revelation. On a machine like the Zero DSR/X, a well-planned loop of 90 to 130 miles with a charge stop or two is entirely realistic, and the routes below are designed to make range anxiety a thing of the past.

The single biggest change from petrol touring is that you plan the ride around the chargers rather than the fuel stations, and the good news is that the UK charging network has grown enormously. Before you set off, it is well worth reading my dedicated guide to electric bike charging in the UK, which covers connector types, networks and apps. Get the charging sorted and electric touring becomes genuinely liberating.

Understanding Real-World Range

The first rule of electric route planning is to be honest about range. Manufacturer figures are city-cycle optimistic. On flowing A and B roads at a spirited pace, expect to see meaningfully less, and a motorway blast will drain the battery fastest of all. That is actually good news for route planning, because the best electric motorcycle routes favour exactly the kind of flowing rural roads where an electric bike is both most efficient and most fun. Plan your legs at around 70 percent of the claimed range and you will always arrive at the charger with a comfortable buffer.

Surrey Hills City-to-Countryside Loop

Close to London, the Surrey Hills make an ideal first electric adventure because you are never far from a charger and the roads are gloriously efficient for an EV. A 70-mile loop from the edge of the capital out through Dorking, along the A25 and over the wooded greensand lanes near Wotton keeps you off fast dual carriageways and on flowing, efficient roads where regenerative braking tops the battery back up on every downhill.

Box Hill is the natural halt, and the National Trust visitor centre area has EV charging as well as the famous cafe culture around Ryka's. Charge while you enjoy a coffee and you barely notice the stop. This is the perfect route to learn how your bike behaves and how much range those flowing roads really return. For more escapes in this direction, see my weekend routes from London guide.

South Downs and Coast Blast (A272 to the Sea)

A city-to-coast run is one of the great pleasures of electric riding, and the A272 across Sussex delivers it beautifully. The road flows west to east through Petersfield, Midhurst and Haywards Heath with long sweeping bends that suit the instant electric torque perfectly. Drop south towards the coast at Brighton or Chichester and you have a superb 90-mile day with a charge stop at the seaside.

Both Brighton and Chichester have plentiful rapid chargers, so you can top up over lunch by the sea before the return leg. The efficiency of the rolling South Downs terrain means you will likely arrive with more charge than you expected. My South Downs motorcycle route guide covers the best of these roads. Plan the charge stop into your lunch and the day flows seamlessly.

Range anxiety is really just planning anxiety in disguise. Spend ten minutes the night before mapping your charge stops and the fear evaporates. An electric bike on a well-planned route is one of the most relaxing ways to travel that I know.

The Cotswolds Silent Wander

The Cotswolds and electric motorcycles are a match made in heaven. The gentle gradients keep energy use low, the modest speed limits maximise your range, and the near-silent running lets you drink in the peace of the honey-stone villages without shattering it with exhaust noise. A 75-mile loop taking in Stow-on-the-Wold, Bourton-on-the-Water and Burford is comfortably within range of most modern electric machines with a single midday top-up.

Charging has improved dramatically across the region, with rapid units now in the larger towns and destination chargers at many attractions and hotels. Stow-on-the-Wold and Cirencester both have public chargers near their central car parks. My detailed Cotswolds touring routes guide maps the loop, and the silence of an electric bike genuinely enhances the timeless atmosphere of these villages.

Peak District Efficient Dales Loop

The Peak District might sound like hard work for an electric bike, but the White Peak dales around Bakewell are surprisingly efficient thanks to all that regenerative braking on the descents. Every downhill puts charge back into the battery, so a loop that undulates through the limestone dales can return better real-world range than a flat motorway run. A 65-mile loop linking Bakewell, Tideswell and Ashbourne is a rewarding and efficient day out.

Bakewell has become a sensible charging hub with rapid units near the main car parks, so you can top up while enjoying the famous pudding. Plan your loop to start and finish here and you have a natural charge point built into the day. My Peak District roads guide has the wider picture if you want to explore further afield.

Mitigating Range Anxiety on the Road

A few habits transform electric touring from nervous to relaxed. These are the ones I rely on:

  • Plan charge stops before you leave. Use a charging app to identify rapid units on your route and have a backup for each one.
  • Charge to 80 percent, not 100. The last 20 percent charges slowest, so on a multi-stop day you cover more miles by topping up little and often.
  • Use regen wisely. Strong regenerative braking on descents genuinely extends your range, so let the bike harvest energy.
  • Favour flowing roads. A and B roads are far more efficient than sustained high-speed dual carriageway running.
  • Keep navigation clear. A secure Oxford CLIQR Phone Mount keeps your charging app and route in view at all times.

For a deeper look at the practicalities, my guide to electric motorcycle touring in the UK covers longer trips and multi-day planning in detail.

The Best Electric Bikes for These Routes

The right machine makes electric touring a joy. The Zero DSR/X is my standout pick for these routes, an adventure-styled electric with genuine touring range, a comfortable riding position and the flexibility to tackle everything from the Surrey Hills to the Peak District dales. Its efficient powertrain and regenerative braking make the most of the flowing roads these loops are built around.

Electric motorcycle technology is advancing quickly, and range figures improve with every model year. For a current overview of the market, see my guide to the best electric motorcycles of 2026. Whichever machine you choose, the best electric motorcycle routes in the UK reward careful planning with silent, torque-rich riding that reveals the countryside in a whole new way. Sort your charging, respect your range and enjoy the quiet revolution.
